extracted.intended_audience: NBA fans, sports-news readers, and people following the trade deadline
extracted.subtask_description: Live/recap coverage of NBA trade-deadline activity that reports transactions, attributes sources, explains motivations, and analyzes roster/financial impacts. Intended as a running tracker with updates, links, and context for readers following deals in real time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly attribute every report to its source (e.g., 'first reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania', 'reports Anthony Slater of ESPN', 'sources said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly credits specific reporters and outlets (Shams Charania, The Athletic, ESPN, etc.) and notes when stories are 'broken' or 'confirmed.' Good practice: indicate who reported the news, whether it's been confirmed, and link to the original report when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full transaction specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: List the concrete elements of each deal: players involved, draft picks (with years), cash considerations, and additional components (e.g., trade exceptions, protections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article: 'Clippers are sending Ivica Zubac and Kobe Brown to Indiana for Bennedict Mathurin, Isaiah Jackson, two first-round picks and one second-round pick'; include protections (e.g., 'protected 1-4 and 10-30') and mention exact dollar amounts when reported (e.g., '$3.5 million').

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the purpose/motivation of the deal
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the trade happened (financial reasons, roster fit, clearing roster spots, creating trade exceptions, luxury tax avoidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common phrasing: 'The purpose of the deal was for Boston to get out of the luxury tax', 'made for financial reasons', 'to create a roster spot so they could convert two-way player Dominick Barlow to a standard contract.' A good tracker states the stated or likely motivation behind moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary-cap and luxury-tax implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how a transaction affects team payroll, luxury tax status, repeater tax exposure, and other cap mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article references teams 'getting out of the luxury tax', 'duck the tax', and 'repeater tax' consequences. Guidance: include whether a move is designed to save money, avoid tax penalties, or create cap flexibility and mention relevant figures where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract status and roster mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Note contract details relevant to the move: expiring contracts, team/player options, two-way conversions, waivers, buyouts, and whether a team will waive or flip a player.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'will be waived in 3-team deal', 'player option for next season', 'convert two-way player to a standard contract.' Explain next administrative steps and likely immediate outcomes for the player (waived, bought out, converted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Player role, recent usage, and statistical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the player's recent role, minutes, season averages, shooting percentages, and how they fit (or don't) in their new team's rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives examples like 'Tillman had been out of the rotation, averaging 7.9 minutes per game', 'Thomas has ... averaged 15.6 points per game, but on just 39.9% shooting.' Good reporting ties transaction to on-court performance and likely role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team strategy and longer-term roster planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how a trade fits into the team's short-term goals (contending vs. tanking), long-term rebuild, or offseason planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes strategic aims: 'Milwaukee should want to tank its way into a better pick', 'The Clippers begin a pivot to whatever comes next at the Intuit Dome', 'Grizzlies are in full rebuild mode.' Guidance: contextualize trades within team timelines and front-office objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft-pick detail and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Report draft-pick years, protections, swaps, and how picks convert or are contingent on protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'the Pacers 2026 first-rounder (protected 1-4 and 10-30) and the 2029 Pacers unprotected first-rounder'; 'converts to a 2031 unprotected first from Indiana.' Report protections and conversion triggers clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate roster/rotation impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the move will change rotations, who gains or loses minutes, and impacts on starting lineups or bench roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page analyzes effects: 'Alvarado ... gives them a tremendous on-ball defender to help back up Jalen Brunson', 'Zubac may set a pick or be in the dunker’s spot' and 'Bulls are overloaded with ball-handling guards.' Good analysis ties the transaction to lineup and minutes shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injury, availability, and health context
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention recent injuries, games missed, and expected availability that affect player value or role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Porzingis ... limited to 17 games this season', 'Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had an abdominal strain and could be out through the All-Star break.' Include injury timelines and how they influence a team's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mechanics explanation (multi-team deals, exceptions, swaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain complex mechanics of three-team trades, trade exceptions, pick swaps, and multi-step transactions so readers understand how the pieces move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article breaks down three-team deals and why teams reroute players (e.g., 'three-team deal that allows Jazz to pick up two seconds, the Hawks to land ... and the Cavaliers to shed significant salary'). Guidance: clarify each team's inbound/outbound assets and the administrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, possible follow-ups, and expected next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether further moves are likely (buyouts, flips, more trades) and set expectations about immediate next steps (e.g., 'expect the Barlow contract announcement in the next 24 hours', 'Toronto will not require CP3 to report and will work to flip him').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tracker frequently notes expected administrative actions or additional trades following a primary move. Use phrasing that signals certainty level (expect, likely, possible) and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of embedded/social-media sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed or quote social-media posts and tweets from insiders as primary or supporting evidence, with clear attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes tweet embeds and quotes (e.g., Shams Charania tweets). Guidance: include embedded tweets when they provide breaking info, but label them as the reporter's post and corroborate when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of reporting and analysis/tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix factual reporting of transactions with concise analysis and clear opinion/interpretation markers; maintain professionalism and avoid overstating certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article alternates play-by-play transaction recaps with analysis ('This is as high as his value has ever been', 'That has put the Lakers in a tight spot'). Best practice: separate fact (the deal) from interpretation and flag speculation ('reports', 'sources say', 'expect').

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of broader league implications and rival offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss how a move affects league-wide dynamics or other teams' strategies (who's still in a chase, who is out, and how offers compare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The Warriors plan to keep Draymond Green', 'Minnesota out of Giannis chase (for now)', 'The Bucks are sifting through proposals specifically from the Heat, Wolves, Knicks and Warriors.' Good coverage positions the trade inside the wider market.
